profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at an asset-management firm between the research team and the productization team after a successful internal study on forecasting the next FOMC rate move. The firm wants to turn the study into a recurring monthly signal used by macro strategists and risk managers. The immediate context is that the research prototype showed an AUC of 0.83 using TF-IDF features from FOMC texts plus macro indicators in XGBoost, and now the two workstreams need to align on interfaces, handoffs, artifact ownership, and what will be delivered before the next FOMC meeting cycle. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the 'monthly forecast package,' which dataset/version will be used, how the research notebook transitions into an operational deliverable, and what counts as the model being 'ready' for downstream consumption. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the handoff plan for the next cycle: Elena will supply the model package and documentation, Marcus will wire it into the internal rates dashboard, and both believe they have settled timing, content, and ownership details for the rollout.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Machine learning for macro forecasting, text-based feature engineering, model evaluation
members.background: Elena leads a small quantitative research group inside the firm's cross-asset strategy unit and previously worked in academic econometrics before moving into buy-side research.
members.private_state: She wants the prototype to be adopted quickly without reopening methodological debates, and she is trying to preserve the exact research conditions that produced the headline result while minimizing extra packaging work for her team.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'monthly forecast,' they mean the research team's event-level probability for the next scheduled FOMC decision, refreshed once per month for internal review.
The 'current dataset' is the frozen research snapshot finalized after the backtest sign-off in early May, because reproducibility matters more than pulling the latest revised macro vintages.
A model is 'ready' once the probability output is stable on the holdout process and accompanied by feature notes; downstream visualization and monitoring are separate implementation tasks.
The 'handoff deck' naturally includes model score, top SHAP drivers, and a one-page methodology note, but not raw feature tables or a production-style data dictionary.

members.name: Marcus Hale
members.expertise: Internal data products, dashboard delivery, stakeholder coordination, operational rollout
members.background: Marcus manages internal research tools used by portfolio managers and risk teams and previously worked in enterprise data operations supporting market and economic data pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants a smooth rollout into the existing rates dashboard with minimal follow-up questions from users, and he is trying to secure enough structure and documentation so his team does not inherit ambiguous ownership later.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'monthly forecast,' they mean the signal displayed in the dashboard each month and kept current through the meeting date, including any off-cycle updates if new inputs arrive.
The 'current dataset' is whatever the firm-standard macro pipeline exports at runtime, including any benchmark revisions and the latest parsed Fed communication files.
A model is 'ready' only when it can be consumed by downstream users without manual interpretation, including field definitions, lineage, and dashboard-ready output formatting.
The 'handoff deck' is shorthand for the full implementation packet the platform team usually receives: sample outputs, schema, ownership notes, and exceptions handling.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to deliver the monthly forecast before each FOMC cycle.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a single event-focused forecast for the next scheduled FOMC decision, regenerated on the monthly research cadence.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means a dashboard signal that stays current throughout the month and can reflect late-arriving updates close to the meeting.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'monthly forecast' sounds like an ordinary cadence label rather than a scope boundary, so both assume the phrase is already operationally obvious.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'current dataset' is being handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the model should run on the current dataset.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the frozen May research snapshot used for the validated backtest and feature extraction.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is referring to the live firm data feed's latest macro vintages and most recent ingested Fed text files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both routinely use 'current dataset' to mean the obvious active source in their own workflows, and because the meeting is about coordination rather than methodology, neither thinks to name the specific snapshot or pipeline.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the model being 'ready'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the package should be ready for the dashboard team next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes 'ready' means research-approved outputs are stable, reproducible, and interpretable enough for downstream teams to pick up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus believes 'ready' means the package is operationally complete for immediate integration, including schema details, field definitions, and exception cases.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'ready for the dashboard team' normally signals status alignment, and both are competent professionals accustomed to abstract progress language, so the differing completion thresholds remain hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: How the handoff materials will be delivered
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Elena will send the handoff deck and model package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena plans to send a slide deck, exported model artifact, and a research notebook appendix through the shared research folder.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus expects a structured implementation bundle in the platform team's intake template with CSV examples, schema tabs, and named owners in the ticketing system.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations routinely say 'handoff deck and package' as a familiar phrase, which masks different procedural defaults for transferring work between research and platform teams.
